newsitem.title: UK: Drought to cause lower Thai 97/98 sugar output-Man.
newsitem.headline: Drought to cause lower Thai 97/98 sugar output-Man.

text.p: Sugar production in Thailand for 1997/98 is expected to be less than this season as much of the damage to cane caused by drought is probably irredeemable, trade house E D & F Man said on Monday.
In its latest report, Man said the official estimate for cane production at 49.23 million tonnes suggested final sugar output at 5.07 million tonnes based on a factory sugar yield of 10.3 percent.
This year's sugar output totalled 5.8 million tonnes.
But the Man report noted that Thai farmers said the estimate for cane production was lower than that released by the Cane and Sugar Board.
Those millers most affected by the drought from May to July would try to delay the start of crushings as much as possible to give the cane a chance to recover.
Although sugar consumption was unlikely to rise much from the 1.67 million tonnes tel quel seen last year, exports would fall significantly to 3.4 million tonnes.
"Millers will attempt to fill their refining capacity, which mneans that it is the raw export volume that will bear the brunt of the fall in production," the report said.
It added that the practice of burning cane would probably continue to hound Thailand's sugar industry unless it could make significant progress with mechanisation.
The practice was likely to depress factory sugar yields and keep them at levels under 10.5 percent.
